Both sets are RATCHETS over a measured population, not licences: the guard asserts them in BOTH directions, so an entry whose file has stopped offending reds the guard until the entry is deleted. The write set pins a MULTISET of licensed destinations — pinning only the count let three legitimate fixture writes be SUBSTITUTED for three `tests/*.tmp.ts` writes, and pinning only the destinations let a licensed write be DUPLICATED, both with the guard still green. The leak set pins counts per file, so a new leak inside an already-listed file reds too.

packages/kn-next/src/__tests__/adapter-d.reason: Boots a REAL `next dev` server against a checked-in fixture project, so these three destinations — the generated `.knext/adapter.mjs` bundle, its `.gitignore`, and the `node_modules/@types` symlink parent — have to sit inside that project. Next resolves a project by directory, and a dev server rooted at a temp copy would no longer be exercising the tracked fixture the test names. Not the #918 shape either: nothing here writes a transient `.ts` into `tests/`, which is what raced the typecheck gate. The licence is these three EXPRESSIONS: any other destination in this file, including one substituted for one of these, is a red.

unremovedTempDirs.note: Unremoved `mkdtemp` sites, measured when the LIFETIME half of this guard landed (D9): originally 157 across 47 files. Burn-down tracked in #939 — the first pass paired 35 sites across 30 files with an `rmSync` (try/finally, an `afterAll`/`afterEach` drain over a registry, or a direct removal), leaving 122 across 17 files below. Each pairing shrank this ceiling in the SAME change that fixed it, because the guard reds a file that stopped leaking but stayed on the list. The remainder is deferred, not licensed: fixing every site means touching files across every package, and a guard that lands with its subject already red teaches people to disable it. This list is a CEILING: a file may only leak fewer than it does today, never more, and a file that stops leaking must leave the list. Nothing may be added to it — a new leak is a red, including a new leak in a file already here and a new leak that reuses a binding name already here. That last clause was FALSE when it was first written: a leak whose name collided with a drained iteration's loop element rode free, because that loop's own `rmSync(d)` was counted a second time as a direct removal. Measured against the pre-fix scan by appending a probe leak under each loop-element name: 12 (file, name) pairs, of which 8 were closed by excluding drain bodies from direct credit and 4 more needed that exclusion widened to loops over a non-identifier iterable (`of [appDir]`, `of dirs.splice(0)`). 0 remain. The guard proves the claim on the colliding name rather than on a name chosen to pass.
